svg.title: Neural Network Field Guide

text.font-family: Poppins, 'Avenir Next', 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
Lato, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 42 architectures and training schemes, from the perceptron (1958) to diffusion LLMs (2025).

text.font-family: Lato, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Each diagram draws a network in miniature, from input at the bottom to output at the top. In most panels, a circle is one neuron; in sequence models, a column is a token and a circle

text.font-family: Lato, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: its whole vector at one layer. A square is larger: an image patch, a matrix-valued state, a whole network (in gray). Color and mark both show a cell’s role, so diagrams read without color.

text.font-family: Lato, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Faded parts play little or no role in the step shown. Parts repeated over positions, windows, copies, or passes share weights; layers, experts, encoders, and decoders drawn alike do not.

text.font-family: Lato, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Sections group by a defining trait: wiring, dynamics, training, cost, or purpose. Years and training methods follow landmark papers, not always the first; many can be trained other ways.
